body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- Astra initially looked capable of threatening Fable; with Opus 5.5, my preference has shifted to Opus on both value and finished output
- Opus has 60% lower standard input/output token rates than Astra, and Anthropic reports a FrontierCode lead at lower task cost; that supports the choice without proving a win on every task
- Below are actual public project screenshots with source and license links: inspect the work, then compare both models on your own acceptance criteria

## Astra put Fable under pressure. Opus changed my choice

- My first impression of Astra was that even Fable had a serious challenger. OpenAI's published AutomationBench comparison put Astra at 41.4% and Fable 5.1 at 31.4%; this measured business-workflow completion, not every kind of intelligence ([OpenAI launch](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/))
- Since Opus 5.5 arrived, my verdict is simpler: **Opus wins my vote on both value and finished output**. That is my assessment, not a controlled personal benchmark or a claim that every reader will see the same result
- The interesting change is the combination: a lower rate alongside output I prefer. Being impressive at launch earns attention; it does not buy a lifetime exemption from comparison

## Lower rates, and evidence beyond the price tag

Standard API prices in USD per million tokens, checked September 28, 2026. Astra uses OpenAI's short-context tier.

| Model | Fresh input | Output | Calculated example total |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Astra | $10 | $50 | $22.50 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 | $20 | $9.00 |

*Sources: [OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Anthropic pricing](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5)*

- Example: 1 million fresh input tokens plus 250,000 output tokens across requests. Formula: `input / 1m × input rate + output / 1m × output rate`; tools, caching and other processing tiers excluded
- Both listed rates are **60% lower** for Opus: `(10 − 4) / 10 = (50 − 20) / 50`. This is equal-token arithmetic, not a measured 60% saving on a completed project
- Anthropic reports **54.6% for Opus at medium effort versus Astra's top 53.3% on FrontierCode**, at about one-fifth the task cost. The evaluation asks whether code changes would be merged; settings differ, and this is the maker's report ([evaluation and methodology](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5))
- Its AutomationBench table also has Astra at **41.4% versus Opus at 40.0%**. A blanket victory would misread the same evidence; benchmark tables do not become opinion polls just because I have a favorite

## Actual outputs: two public projects you can inspect

These are the creators' repository screenshots, resized and encoded as WebP. They were not regenerated for this article. **Different prompts, tools, assets and development histories mean they are showcases, not a matched contest.** Model attribution follows each project's public record; I did not independently reproduce the builds.

### Astra: Sunward, a coastal driving game

![Sunward driving screenshot with a purple car, coastal road, minimap and speedometer](/media/c015e5dd-f77a-487e-9bc0-1e1fc46182b2.webp)

*Source: [Sunward project](https://github.com/yjrocks712/Sunward-by-GPT-6-Astra) — original driving screenshot; © 2026 Sunward contributors, MIT. [Screenshot permission and third-party notices](https://github.com/yjrocks712/Sunward-by-GPT-6-Astra/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) · [Preserved license notices](/licenses/astra-opus-examples.txt)*

- The public development notes attribute the Unity game to an interactive Codex session with GPT-6 Astra; the repository includes source and a Mac release
- What is visible: a navigable-looking road scene, vehicle, minimap, speed display and radio interface assembled into one game screen. A still image cannot verify handling, frame rate or bug-free play
- This is a concrete reason Astra drew attention: the example is an inspectable project, not merely a paragraph promising that a game could exist

### Opus 5.5: Tidewater, a coastal fishing world

![Tidewater screenshot showing a fishing rod, wooden pier, translucent ocean and cloud-lit coast](/media/aa900b25-a699-4ba6-b6d5-429d5fe9728a.webp)

*Source: [dgreenheck / Tidewater](https://github.com/dgreenheck/tidewater) — original repository screenshot; © 2026 DRG Software Solutions LLC, MIT code and associated documentation. [Asset credits](https://github.com/dgreenheck/tidewater/blob/main/CREDITS.md) · [Preserved license notices](/licenses/astra-opus-examples.txt) · [Browser demo](https://dgreenheck.github.io/tidewater/)*

- The creator describes the project as built with Opus 5.5. The current repository is a WebGPU fishing game with its own renderer; its credits also identify reused assets, so the finished image is not evidence that the model made every ingredient
- What catches my eye here is the coherent lighting, translucent water, pier detail and fishing viewpoint. This is the sort of finished presentation I value; the screenshot does not establish how much of that difference comes from the model
- Try the linked demo or inspect its source if this kind of output matters to you. A beautiful screenshot is a good invitation, but it still cannot click the buttons for you

## My default is Opus; Astra still gets the difficult second opinion

- I would start with Opus 5.5 when the job needs a finished artifact: its rate advantage is explicit, and its output is my current preference
- For a stubborn design or reasoning problem, I would give Astra the same requirements and compare the result. Keep the tools, effort settings and retry budget visible rather than calling two unrelated screenshots a benchmark
- Count **total API spend / accepted tasks**, including failed attempts; log human review minutes separately. A lower rate matters most when the result actually passes

## Community Reactions

- In an r/codex discussion, the author called Opus productive but preferred Astra and Fable for deep async-runtime architecture. That is a useful limit on the claim that Opus wins everything ([original discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1wpveoe/astra_vs_opus_55_my_impressions_on_hard_project/))
- In the same thread, another commenter reported that Opus fixed a bot problem while Astra used substantial quota without fixing it. This supports a different experience, not a verified API-cost comparison or a community consensus ([original discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1wpveoe/astra_vs_opus_55_my_impressions_on_hard_project/))

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q: Do the screenshots prove Opus is better at graphics?**
  - No; the projects use different engines, assets, prompts and iteration histories. They show real published artifacts, not a controlled ranking
- **Q: Is the 60% difference what I will save on a project?**
  - Only the listed token rates are 60% lower. Token counts, cache use, retries and tools determine the actual bill; subscriptions are separate
- **Q: Can I reuse these examples?**
  - Follow the linked licenses and retain required notices; Sunward explicitly includes screenshots in its MIT grant, while Tidewater also lists separate third-party asset terms. Permission extends only to rights the licensors hold
title: Why I Switched from GPT-6 Astra to Opus 5.5
description: Astra challenged Fable; Opus 5.5 now wins my vote on value and finished work. Official rates, evaluation limits and real open-source project screenshots.
imageAlt: Notebook showing Astra challenging Fable and Opus 5.5 favored for lower rates and finished work
